transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in today because... lately, I've had to be a lot more in front of people for my job. I help plan events, so I'm around crowds and cameras a lot. And I just can't stop staring at this one uneven-looking part of my face in photos. 

It's really bothering me. Everyone else tells me they barely see anything at all when I point it out, but... I just can't stop focusing on it.
Can you tell me roughly how much time each day you spend thinking about or checking on that part of your face—like looking in mirrors, taking photos, or trying to cover it up?

It's hard to put an exact number of hours on it, but it takes up a lot of my day. Like, before I send out event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I'll just keep checking my face in my phone camera. I end up having to retake photos over and over, or I'll practice tilting my head a certain way so it doesn't look as uneven. Sometimes I even ask a coworker if I look weird. It just... it eats up enough time that I actually start falling behind on my planning stuff.
Aside from concerns about your face, do you ever have other repeated, unwanted thoughts or urges to perform certain rituals or checks that aren't related to how you look?

No, not really. I mean, I don't have any other rituals or anything like that. It's really just the stuff with my face that I get stuck on. I don't have any other repeated thoughts or checks that aren't about how I look.
When people tell you they don't notice any unevenness, how convinced are you that they're wrong and that the flaw is really there?

I mean... I'm pretty convinced they're wrong. I know they say they don't see it, but when I look in the mirror or at pictures, it's right there. It's so obvious to me. So, yeah, I feel like they're either just trying to be nice or they aren't looking closely enough, because to me, it's definitely real.

Aside from how you feel about your face, have you noticed any other strong beliefs or suspicions lately—like feeling that people are watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you in some way?

No, I don't have anything like that. I don't feel like people are out to get me or watching me or anything... I mean, unless I'm worrying that they're staring at my face, but that's just because of how it looks. But no other weird suspicions or anything else.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things, or had other sensory experiences that other people don't seem to notice or hear?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. Nothing like that at all.
Is there any part of you, even a small part, that wonders if your perception of the unevenness might be exaggerated or not entirely accurate?

Um... not really. I mean, I guess maybe for a split second if everyone around me is saying they don't see it, I might wonder why we're seeing two different things. But... then I look in the mirror or check my phone camera, and it's just right there. So, no, I don't really think I'm exaggerating it. I'm just seeing what's actually on my face.
